comment: B4 Round 25 — history-visibility scope vectors. Spec authority: data-structures/history-visibility.md + authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md. The history_visibility cell (cas-register, cx:cell:cx.component.realm.history_visibility.v1:<space_id>) holds one of {joined, invited, world_readable, shared}. The reducer projects the timeline differently per viewer based on their (membership_state, history_visibility, event_origin_ts vs viewer_join_ts). 'joined' (default): only events at-or-after the viewer's last join_ts are visible. 'invited': events at-or-after the viewer's invite_ts are visible (allows pre-accept preview). 'world_readable': all events visible to anyone who can reach the cell, even non-members. 'shared': events from the moment the visibility setting first turned 'shared' onward are visible to non-members; events prior remain joined-scoped. Redacted events compose with visibility (see redaction_history_visibility_fixture for the cross-product); admin override uses the recovery_capability surface to expose audit-view of any single event_id regardless of viewer scope.

vectors.name: joined_default_member_sees_only_post_join_events
vectors.comment: Default visibility 'joined': member alice joined at ts=100; an event at ts=50 (pre-join) MUST NOT be in her timeline projection; an event at ts=150 (post-join) MUST be visible.

expected.rationale: joined visibility hides events with origin_ts < viewer.join_ts.

vectors.name: invited_pre_accept_preview_visible
vectors.comment: history_visibility=invited: bob has membership_state=invite with invite_ts=120. Events at ts=130 (post-invite, pre-accept) MUST be visible for preview; events at ts=110 (pre-invite) MUST be hidden.

expected.rationale: invited visibility uses invite_ts as the cutoff (allows pre-accept preview of post-invite history).

vectors.name: world_readable_non_member_sees_everything
vectors.comment: history_visibility=world_readable: charlie is NOT a member of the space (membership_state=null) but the visibility setting allows everyone to read. All events visible regardless of charlie's join_ts.

expected.rationale: world_readable bypasses membership and join_ts gating; all events are public.

vectors.name: shared_cutover_threshold_applies
vectors.comment: history_visibility transitioned from 'joined' to 'shared' at shared_since_ts=200. Non-member dora viewing later: events at ts=180 (before cutover) MUST be hidden; events at ts=210 (after cutover) MUST be visible.

expected.rationale: shared visibility uses the cutover ts (when the setting was first set to 'shared') as the floor for non-members.

vectors.name: redacted_event_per_viewer_audit_view
vectors.comment: history_visibility=joined; alice (author) gets audit_view of her redacted event with original content; bob (member) only sees the tombstone. Composes redaction reducer with history_visibility scope.

expected.rationale: Authors always see their own original content via audit_view; other members see only the tombstone marker.

vectors.name: admin_override_recovery_capability_exposes_event
vectors.comment: Admin holds cx.recovery.read.history.v1 capability. They request a single event_id even though viewer.join_ts > event.origin_ts (joined visibility would otherwise hide it). The override path returns the event under audit_view with explicit override_audit_log entry.

expected.rationale: Admin override via recovery_capability bypasses normal joined-visibility cutoff but mandates audit log.

vectors.name: ban_transition_hides_all_events_in_joined
vectors.comment: Round 26 B4 余下 — viewer eve was a join member who got banned at ts=200. Under history_visibility=joined, banned viewers MUST see no events regardless of their prior join_ts. Even an event at ts=150 (post-original-join, pre-ban) MUST be hidden in the projection.

expected.rationale: Banned viewer state forces a strict deny on joined visibility; admin override is the only way to expose audit data, gated by recovery_capability.

vectors.name: ban_transition_does_not_hide_world_readable
vectors.comment: Round 26 B4 余下 — even banned viewers can still read world_readable history (visibility setting is global; ban only affects member-scoped visibility). Verifies the projection's separation between membership-state gating and world_readable bypass.

expected.rationale: world_readable visibility bypasses all membership gating — banned viewers can still read once the cell is publicly readable.

vectors.name: admin_override_audit_view_for_banned_member
vectors.comment: Round 26 B4 余下 — admin holds cx.recovery.read.history.v1 and uses it to read a specific event for a banned member's investigation. The recovery_capability + audit_log requirement composes: admin sees the original via audit_view + audit_log is emitted. This is a second admin_override vector to cover the more complex investigation flow.

expected.rationale: Recovery capability bypasses ban + joined cutoff for investigation; audit_log binds the read to the admin's DID + the subject_did.

negative_vectors.name: non_member_world_readable_off_rejected
negative_vectors.comment: history_visibility=joined and viewer is a non-member. Even an event at ts=10 must be hidden (not just from the timeline — the projection MUST refuse to expose it).

expected.rationale: joined visibility requires viewer.membership_state=join and join_ts<=event.origin_ts; non-members are denied.

negative_vectors.name: admin_override_without_capability_rejected
negative_vectors.comment: Caller claims admin override but does NOT hold cx.recovery.read.history.v1; the override request MUST be rejected with capability_not_held.

expected.rationale: Recovery override requires explicit capability grant; missing capability MUST refuse the request.
